title: A conversation you can follow
question: Compare three conversation layouts. Each keeps the existing console, adds message attribution and timestamps, and makes live activity visible. Expand a preview to read it at full size. Preview content is illustrative.

options.label: Turn by turn
options.thesis: Keep each request and its replies together, with worker reports nested inside the exchange.
options.viewport: Each exchange starts with your compact request, followed by the lead and attributed worker updates on one left edge.
options.risk: Long exchanges need more scrolling, and each request is less visually separate from its answer.

options.label: Message timeline
options.thesis: Read one chronological timeline with a time gutter and distinct message and activity rows.
options.viewport: All authors share one text column. Time and source stay beside each message, with compact execution summaries between replies.
options.risk: More operational detail competes with the conversation, even when tool output stays collapsed.

options.label: Focused chat
options.thesis: Keep familiar chat bubbles inside one centered reading column, with clear names and times.
options.viewport: Your messages sit on the right of the reading column, not the panel. Agent replies and worker reports carry visible attribution.
options.risk: The slight left-right alternation remains, though both sides share the same narrow column.
